City council approves new bike lanes

By Sam Reporter October 2, 2026

The city council voted seven to two on Tuesday night to fund twelve kilometers of protected bike lanes, the largest expansion of the network since it was created a decade ago.

Supporters said the lanes would make cycling safer for commuters and children riding to school. Opponents argued that removing parking would hurt small businesses along the affected streets.

"We heard from hundreds of residents, and the message was clear," said council member Jordan Lee. "People want to ride, but they do not feel safe sharing the road with heavy traffic."

Construction timeline

Work on the first segment, along River Road, is scheduled to begin in March. The remaining segments will be built in phases over the following two years, with the busiest corridors prioritized.

The project will cost an estimated 18 million, with roughly half covered by a regional transportation grant.
